Hi Priyom — thanks for following up.

Repro steps (short):
1) Client aggregates multiple user messages and system instructions into a single batch payload (~50 items).
2) Many items contain a 6–8 turn history (so token counts vary widely).
3) We POST to /v1/generate with stream=false and wait ~30–45s.
4) On ~10% of large batches we see 500s; when it happens the server memory for the instance (G4) grows ~2–3GB over baseline and doesn’t drop until request completes/evicts.

Attached: brightlane_request_trace.log (contains request_id=br-20260720-1120 and the raw payload), sample_batch_payload.json (trimmed). I also attached a small SDK dump where we capture the client batching configuration.

Let me know if you need anything else — we can do a call at 11:30 PT.

Folks — forwarding BrightLane repro artifacts (attached) and a concise ask. Internal only please.

Summary: BrightLane is hitting intermittent 500s and steady memory growth on host when clients send large batched predict requests (~50 items, mixed token lengths). They POST with stream=false. We see ~10% failure rate on large batches. They included request_id br-20260720-1120 and a sample payload.

Asks: 
1) Can Runtime team reproduce with the attached sample payload and the attached SDK dump?
2) Short-term mitigation: can we suggest a server-side guard (soft-fail with 413 or immediate partial-response fallback) or an SDK change (client-side batch size limit or automatic split) we can push to BrightLane today?
3) Longer-term: is there an SDK flag we can expose that auto-splits by token budget and/or a runtime defensive limit we should add to avoid unbounded KV cache growth? If so, rough ETA and owner.

Links / tracking: INF-3247 (Jira) created to track triage, HubSpot HS-89234.

Priority: High — customer demo cadence impacted.

Thanks — Priyom
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightLane demo follow-up — batch payload behavior

Thanks for the signal and the artifacts, Priyom / Samira. Quick notes from an initial read:

Hypothesis: the root cause looks like KV-cache/context growth combined with long batch durations. When many requests in a single batch contain multi-turn histories, we can blow past expected KV cache TTLs and memory pressure rises, especially if stream=false holds the full response lifecycle and batching prevents early eviction.

Immediate mitigations (can do within 24–48 hrs):
- Runtime: add server-side soft-fail for single request payloads with token_count > 25000 (configurable per-tenant) returning 413 + JSON detail. This avoids host memory blowouts. (owner: Dev, target: 48h)
- SDK: offer a quick client-side flag in next patch (client.auto_split_large_batches = true) that will split payloads into smaller requests by token budget and send as sequential/parallel requests based on user preference. We can ship a patch next week (owner: Karthik, target: next sprint).
- Short-term workaround to recommend to BrightLane: reduce batch size to <= 20 or enable streaming (stream=true) so responses start streaming and runtime can reclaim memory earlier.

Requests for triage:
- Priyom: can you paste the sample payload token counts (per-item) or provide the tokenized totals? That will help set the soft-fail threshold.
- Samira: can you confirm whether BrightLane uses stream=false by default across aggregated batches?

I'll open INF-3247 and add the initial repro steps + a reproducible unit test that hits the kv cache limits (Dev, assigning to you to validate on a small G4 infra). We should also capture memory profile in the repro so we can determine whether this is eviction delay vs leak.

Logan
Principal Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
